## Goal

Bring customer sign-in, account recovery and session handling to one consistent, enforced policy before registration is opened to the public.

## Context

The project applies its own rules (per-account and per-origin request limits, failure records, a common-password check and an extra factor for security changes) in its own server actions, while the authentication library also exposes operations of its own. The two do not apply the same policy. Account-lifecycle and session behaviour have further gaps. The independent review rates the strongest of these P0 and makes the set a condition of opening registration. Details are in the owner's private tracker. Expect three reviewable pull requests on one branch rather than one large change.

## Scope

- PR 1: one policy for every entry point, public or internal, including the behaviour when the rate-limit store is unavailable and when the second factor is switched off. Allow only the operations the product needs; keep verification links working.
- PR 2: account lifecycle — a change of a verified address requires the agreement of the address that is being replaced, and first verification establishes credentials chosen by the mailbox owner and invalidates earlier sessions.
- PR 3: session handling and the account security page — preserve the original creation time and the remembered choice on renewal, apply the absolute limit on every validation path, handle a request for a fresh sign-in, and stop sending a session's own authentication value to the browser.
- `docs/SECURITY.md` records the resulting policy.

## Out of scope

- The administration area (SC-019).
- The request-origin contract (SC-018).
- Paid-zone rendering (SC-008).
- Design changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One policy demonstrably applies to every entry point, proven by tests that call both the public route and the internal action.
- [ ] Each listed lifecycle and session gap has a test that fails before the change and passes after.
- [ ] Registration, verification, sign-in, the second factor, recovery and the account security page all work by hand on staging, in two separate browsers.
- [ ] Independent review approves each of the three pull requests.

## Required tests

- Unit tests per rule.
- A DB test for the account lifecycle.
- A manual staging walkthrough, recorded on the issue.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-017
- SC-018

P0 · Phase A
